name: Pounded Yam
summary: Smooth, stretchy, soft dough made by boiling white yam and pounding it, perfect for scooping soup.
story: Pounded yam, or iyan, is a prized Nigerian swallow, eaten with soups like egusi, efo riro and ogbono. Traditionally it is pounded with a wooden mortar and pestle, which gives a very smooth, elastic texture. It is often served at celebrations and for guests.

items.name: Water
items.amount: enough to just cover the yam

steps.title: Peel and rinse
steps.text: Peel the yam, cut into slices about 3 cm thick, and rinse them in cold water to remove sap. Keep covered in water until ready to boil to prevent browning.

steps.title: Boil the yam
steps.text: Place in a pot with water just covering the yam and bring to a boil. Cook for 20 to 25 minutes until a knife slides through with no resistance.

steps.title: Drain
steps.text: Reserve about 1 cup of the hot cooking water and drain the rest. Work while the yam is still very hot, as cold yam will not become smooth.

steps.title: Pound or mix
steps.text: Pound in a mortar, or use a stand mixer with a dough hook, adding a spoonful of hot water if needed. Keep going for 8 to 10 minutes.

steps.title: Check texture
steps.text: Stop when the dough is smooth, shiny and stretches without lumps. If you see small white lumps, keep pounding.

steps.title: Shape and serve
steps.text: Wet your hands or a bowl, mould the dough into balls, and serve at once with soup.

tips: Pound while the yam is hot; it gets gluey and lumpy as it cools.
Use only the minimum water needed for a smooth dough.
Do not blend in a regular blender; it makes the dough sticky.

swaps.swap: Frozen peeled yam from African shops is fine. Instant pounded yam flour works in a pinch, but it lacks the real texture.
Stand mixer with dough hook or a potato ricer followed by vigorous beating with a wooden spoon.
